target_customer: AI application developers and companies that need retrieval over their own data sources, buying through an API, AWS Bedrock or self-hosting
problem: AI systems need accurate context from many data sources, and standard retrieval is slow and misses relevant information.
business_model: Usage-based API and licensed model deployment (waitlist access per the site)
product_category: AI research lab: agentic retrieval models

founders.name: Maximilian-David Rumpf
founders.background_notes: YC page says he won a German national excellence scholarship; education not stated.

founders.name: Lotte Seifert
education: ETH Zurich, degree in computer science
University of St. Gallen, degree in economics

technical_complexity.rationale: Training models that retrieve and reason over arbitrary data sources, later an agentic search model, is research heavy work for a small team, with compute and data needs well beyond standard application engineering.

defensibility.rationale: A trained model with benchmarked recall and speed is harder to copy than a wrapper, but foundation model labs and search infrastructure vendors can ship competing retrieval models.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not established from sources opened; no acquisition found.

market_need_then: In 2023 the rise of LLM applications created demand for connecting models to private data; sources opened give no spend figures.

identity.logo: Brand colors listed on Brandfetch are blue and gold tones; no logo description from the company.
identity.voice_and_tone: Terse research lab voice with benchmark claims such as 1.9x better recall and 24x faster.

brand_strength.rationale: Short name but a common name, and nothing was found about the brand itself. Research credibility rather than brand drives attention.

outcome_analysis: SID is active and positions itself as an AI research lab with its first agentic retrieval model, SID-1, on a waitlist. Its site lists Y Combinator, Canaan, Rebel and General Catalyst as backers, but no round sizes or dates were found, and no acquisition or shutdown was reported. There is not enough public evidence to judge traction.
notes: Funding seen only on aggregators (about 500K pre-seed or seed, dated Jan or May 2023, YC); the company site names Canaan, Rebel and General Catalyst as backers without amounts. Nothing recorded as a round. Many 'seed round' search hits were about ZeroEntropy, a different company. No dated competitor sources near the batch found. The company site mentions teams in San Francisco and Zurich. Team size is 7 per YC.
